definitions.meaning: to idle is to ... about, doing nothing
British slang, as in 'use your ...', for the head or brain

explanation.definitionFit: Three separate senses of one word: lazing about, a baked lump of bread, and slang for one's brains.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells us to read the phrase from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: wearing only bottoms means no tops

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being right means wearing only the bottom half of an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NO TOPS backwards; 'bottoms up' also suggests a drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is an informal synonym for exactly correct, just right.

clue.text: Why label invested in welcome business for the elderly

indicators.note: something invested in another is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to welcome someone is to greet them
the word why sounds like the letter Y
a label or tag is a mark

explanation.surface: A tag about the question 'why' is put into a greeting to promote trade for pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why' gives the letter Y by sound; the grey market means older shoppers, grey-haired customers.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey market is the commercial sector of older consumers, grey-haired customers with money to spend.

clue.text: Old cook, we hear, strangling manky turkeys though not unknown in 17 19 down

indicators.note: to strangle is to wrap around the neck, so one piece encloses the other
signals that the cook's name is to be taken by its sound, spelt differently

parts.note: Mrs Beeton, the Victorian cookery writer

indicators.note: British slang for grotty or spoiled, so these letters are mangled into a new order
not tells us to leave out the unknown from the word turkeys

parts.note: in algebra an unknown is x, y or z; here y

explanation.surface: A Victorian cook throttles some rotten turkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: Isabella Beeton wrote the classic Victorian household cookery book; 'manky' is British slang for grotty. 'not unknown' removes an algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was a star of silent films, which were shot in monochrome.

clue.text: Part of church, perhaps eastern part

indicators.note: part of a phrase means just a run of letters from inside it

explanation.surface: A church feature is perhaps the eastern end of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'eastern part' in the surface is apt: the apse is usually at the east end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess, usually at the east end, of a church building.

clue.text: Strong male swimmer saves you, an extraordinarily powerful chap

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it, here held inside another piece

parts.note: the vigorous swimming male cell is a sperm
text-speak writes you as U

explanation.surface: A powerful male swimmer rescues someone, a heroic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong male swimmer' paints an athlete but is a cheeky description of a sperm cell.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero is the archetype of a man with superhuman strength.

clue.text: Timely old joke, consuming wine with last of cheese

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the wine sits inside the joke

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An old joke over port and cheese arrives at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune and timely both describe something happening at a convenient moment.

parts.note: a Disney cartoon dog shares his name with a distant body in the solar system, hence out of this world

explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon dog bears the name of the former ninth planet, so the character is literally out of this world.

clue.text: Rich, a right catch in 17 19 down (in the 5 24)

parts.note: rich food is fatty
a buckle is a catch fastening a belt

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is caught on camera in monochrome, one of the Keystone crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is a further hint to the theme: this comedian worked for Keystone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatty Arbuckle was a silent-film comedian, so he appeared in monochrome pictures.

clue.text: Vulgar story about loony set to take ship

indicators.note: about means around, so the story wraps the other letters

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A vulgar tale about a crazy group setting off on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take ship' reads as boarding a vessel, but SS simply follows on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless and vulgar both describe something lacking refinement or decency.

clue.text: Almost a hundred needed to snare a mythical creature

indicators.note: to snare is to trap, so one piece catches the other inside it
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a century is a hundred

explanation.surface: Nearly a hundred are needed to catch a beast of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A centaur is the half-man half-horse being of Greek legend.

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a river bed is its bottom

explanation.surface: A mathematical riddle about the number one and a copper bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: One multiplied by itself three times is still one, so 1 is the cube of 1.
explanation.definitionFit: One raised to the third power equals one, so it stands cubed to itself.

indicators.note: the gemstone is worn around the boy, so he goes inside it

parts.note: an opal is a gemstone
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad adorned with a precious stone looks his finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal and best both mean the most favourable or effective.

clue.text: Studying the lie of the land, happy to go off round first of routes

definitions.text: Studying the lie of the land

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go about another letter
off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged
first of takes the initial letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cheerful traveller sets off around the opening stretch of the road, surveying the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles HAPPYTOGO, and those letters go 'round' R.
explanation.definitionFit: Topography is the mapping and study of the physical features of an area of ground.

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's monarch
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone collects a king and a knight from the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or fact is to learn it.

clue.text: Gone to the dogs, walk behind cat like Felix?

definitions.text: Gone to the dogs, walk behind cat like Felix?

parts.words: Gone to the dogs, walk behind cat like Felix?
parts.note: a whisky famous for two Scottie dogs on its label, a zebra crossing walk, and the cartoon cat Felix all share one two-tone colour scheme

explanation.definitionFit: The whisky brand with the two terrier mascots, a zebra crossing and Felix the Cat are all monochrome, two-toned.

indicators.note: not beginning means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: An instruction not to take the first step.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the one on a playing card or die.

definitions.meaning: a secretary is a PA, so the two letters spelt out with the word 'and' between them
an animal with fur of the two theme colours

explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda has black-and-white fur, so it fits the theme.

indicators.note: the piece is placed inside the document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A section of a document is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Debited means deducted from an account, money taken off the balance.

clue.text: Bit of a swine's constant abuse of kings

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant

indicators.note: abuse means mistreatment, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A pig is persistently mistreated by monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of a swine' is the definition: a pig's skin is part of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hide of a hog is part of the animal, also used for leather and footballs.

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
rid means freed of something

explanation.surface: Releasing something that smells rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrid means rotten and stinking, a stronger form of foul.

clue.text: Tile on the slant bringing bird death, tragically

parts.note: a cock is a male bird

indicators.note: tragically suggests events going badly wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A slipping roof slate kills a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is slang for a hat; 'tragically' scrambles DEATH to EDHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocked hat is one with turned-up brims; tile is old slang for headgear, and cocked means tilted.

definitions.meaning: a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A cloak worn by the superhero, and a promontory such as one of Cornwall's headlands.

clue.text: Organ loft oft vacated for nobleman

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the word oft moves out of loft

explanation.surface: An organ loft often left empty of a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British noble rank, between viscount and marquess.

parts.note: a ward is a minor under legal guardianship

explanation.surface: A minor legal settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a sum granted in settlement of a claim.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom upward, backwards

parts.note: slang: went to the toilet, peed

explanation.surface: Someone who was low and then rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep voice or note is a low one.

indicators.note: between means placed in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: the Po is an Italian river
R is the abbreviation for river
LA is the abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: A frozen state lying between two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar describes the icy regions round the poles, hence frozen.

clue.text: Disease to keep off one part of the body

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the disease holds the other piece inside

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis
meat that is off is high
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disease that prevents a single part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur, the upper leg bone, is a part of the body.
